title: They wouldn't build the game so I did it for them
author: Material-Watercress1
selftext: I was scrolling TikTok earlier today when I came across this video of a cozy puzzle game about untangling ropes. The comments were all saying that the actual game they link to is nothing like what's shown. That inspired me to take a crack at it myself. I gave the screenshot to Astra and got this game in a single prompt (Plus a handful more prompts for refining and bug fixes).

comments.author: jcarlosn
comments.body:
It looks really promising, and the visuals look great, but the interaction does seem a bit laggy, even though you're not running it on a mobile device (judging by the form factor).

The reason the original game isn't like this is that calculating the threads/strings and their collisions is extremely computationally expensive. It quickly becomes laggy and scales very poorly. It's a game that doesn't exist because of technical limitations, not artistic ones.

You can build a demo that looks like it works, but in practice it will always feel sluggish, scale poorly, and have bugs that are practically impossible to fix. It's fundamentally unreliable because, as the simulation scales up, missed ticks cause strings to pass straight through each other.

You could try discussing these problems with Astra. You'll probably find that the solutions you arrive at look very similar to the ones the original developer must have implemented. And that's essentially why people complain that the game doesn't look or behave like this: it's not that they don't want it to. It's that, with current technology, it simply can't.
